title: Bounded execution of a conditional
statement: Fix a program environment, resource limits, and execution depth. Let $c$ be a condition safe in an initial state $\sigma$, and let $s_1,s_2$ be statements. Suppose that if $c$ holds in $\sigma$, then $s_1$ can execute from $\sigma$ with cost at most $T-(\mathrm{cost}(c)+1)$ to a state satisfying $Q$; suppose likewise that if $c$ does not hold, then $s_2$ can execute with that cost bound to a state satisfying $Q$. If $\mathrm{cost}(c)+1\le T$, the conditional with branches $s_1,s_2$ can execute from $\sigma$ with cost at most $T$ to a state satisfying $Q$.
